description.narrative: The project will help transform two national parks in Khuvsgul and Khentii aimags (provinces) as models for economically inclusive tourism and conservation in the protected area network, by improving park infrastructure, sanitation, and capacity to manage tourism growth sustainably. The designs emphasize tourism benefits for communities, protection of natural capital, and climate-resilient facilities; and scale up from previous grant projects in each park.

Output: Waste management improved Indicator: Two wastewater treatment plants in KLNP and one wastewater treatment storage system at CKTC are constructed with total treatment capacity of 135 m3/day Achievement: 1 Progress/Status: On track. Two WWTPs completed (Khatgal, Khankh) with total capacity of 105 m3/day. For the CKTC, design scope revised to a waste collection and transfer facility as a soum WWTP was independently constructed by the government. CKTC system: design capacity of 80 m3; work underway and will be completed in Q3 2025 in line with completion of CKTC. Khankh WWTP not yet operational. Actions: (i) re-mobilize project consulting support to strengthen O&M capacity; (ii) seek aimag start-up financing (already provided to Khatgal WWTP). Data Source: MET, KLNP, and OBNP annual reports; Local Authorization for State Inspection reports; engineering company reports; and project technical and progress reports

Output: Inclusive planning and capacity for community-based tourism enhanced Indicator: At least 75% (787) of tour camp employees are residents of Khuvsgul and/or Khentii aimags Achievement: 220 Progress/Status: The eco-certification program was developed and piloted for 4 tour camps and 1 ger camp in 2023. This included an ecotourism capacity assessment of the 5 camps. Six workshop trainings were implemented at KLNP and OBNP. A guideline and handbook for eco-certification of the pilot camps were developed. MET facilitated kickoff meetings to introduce the program; and issued certification of the camps. As of Q4 2025 there has been no further progress. PIU is requested to (i) include the target in the PPMS, (ii) include an update on status in the QPR. To be assessed by field survey in Q2 2026. Data Source: MET, KLNP, OBNP, and soum annual reports; project technical and progress reports; workshop and/or training attendance forms; and reports on participant surveys

As of February 2025, about 9,626 residents at KLNP and OBNP [100% of the population of Khatgal (3,644 people), Khankh (2,854) and Dadal soum (3,128) in 2024] are benefiting from the new WWTPs and landfills. About 3,057 households (about 11,009 residents) derive livelihoods from tourism in the KLNP and OBNP, including about 50% women Achievement: 5000 Progress/Status: Status unclear. The indicator has not been clearly tracked. At midterm mission (June 2025), PIU was requested to (i) include the target in the PPMS, (iii) include an update on status in the QPR for Q3 2025. This task is still pending due to national changes in the composition of PIUs, which has delayed recruitment of a new PIU M&E position. Task rescheduled to Q2 2026.
Background information: as of Q4 2025, a total of 3,430 residents have received the tourism skills training for job placement at KLNP and OBNP under the project. As of Q4 2025, six out 11 CP packages were completed. Four contracts are ongoing. These were expected to be completed by the end of 2025 but due to inclement weather and new potential safeguard risks, have been delayed. Completion expected by Q2 2026. Data Source: MET, KLNP, OBNP, and soum annual reports; and project technical and progress reports

KLNP and OBNP meet the social, environmental, and sustainability criteria of, and are nominated for, the IUCN Green List of Protected Conserved Areas Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Status unclear. The indicator has not been tracked. PIU requested to: (i) include the target in the PPMS, and (ii) engage a protected area specialist (under CS14) in 2026 to lead review and recommendations. Final assessment for this target will be included in the domestic completion report. Target to be assessed by field survey in Q2 2026. Pending the result, MCSTY and MECC will assess whether to submit a nomination for listing of the KLNP and OBNP on the IUCN Green List of Protected Conserved Areas.
Early project achievement: Under the project, both parks were registered in the UNESCO World Network of Biosphere Reserves of the Man and the Biosphere (MAB): KLNP in 2022 and OBNP in 2023 (the latter during the 35th session of the MAB International Coordinating Council). Data Source: MET, KLNP, OBNP, and soum annual reports; and project technical and progress reports Base year: 2018 Baseline value: N

Tourism planning and management for the KLNP and OBNP are regulated by, and comply with, the revised park management and soum (county) development plans, especially social targets and environmental standards Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Slow progress.
